data.name: HelpIntro
data.value: SnapZap finds duplicates, blurry photos and explicit content in a folder, then writes the set you keep somewhere clean.

data.name: StartStep1
data.value: Scan a folder. Type or paste its path and press Scan. SnapZap reads every photo under it and remembers what it found.

data.name: StartStep2
data.value: Duplicates are found automatically the moment the scan ends — no button to press. The rail's Plan tab shows a Review N groups button once they're ready; optionally press Run under Content review to flag explicit photos.

data.name: StartStep3
data.value: Pick the photos you want to keep. Click them, or use Select all N shown at the top of the grid.

data.name: StartStep4
data.value: Press Export… to write them somewhere clean — or Delete… to recycle what you don't want.

data.name: StartNoteTitle
data.value: Two things that are always true

data.name: StartNoteFolder
data.value: Your original folder is never touched unless you explicitly ask — an export in Move mode, or the opt-in "also recycle what I didn't pick" box.

data.name: StartNoteDelete
data.value: Nothing is ever hard-deleted. Deleting goes to the Recycle Bin, and every batch is reversible from History.

data.name: StartTopBarDesc
data.value: Jump to anything (search by filename or folder), History, and icons for Extract, Help and Setup.

data.name: StartRailDesc
data.value: The library summary and progress strip, above three tabs: Plan (what's done, what's next, and the buttons to run each step), Folders (the folder tree — click one to show only its photos), and Filters (narrow by duplicates, explicit content, sharpness, folder or year).

data.name: StartGridHeaderDesc
data.value: Select all N shown (with a menu for Flagged / Not sure / Keepers), the active filter as a clearable chip, and Sort.

data.name: StartBottomBarDesc
data.value: Export…, Delete… and Hide in Image…, plus Invert / Clear — it appears once you have selected at least one photo.

data.name: StartGearDesc
data.value: Setup: the optional add-on, what duplicate detection checks, and the catalogue.

data.name: ScanIntroP1
data.value: The first time, type or paste a folder path and press Scan, or just press Enter. A leading ~ expands to your home folder. Once a library is loaded, Change folder… under the Scan step in the Plan tab does the same thing for a different folder.

data.name: ScanIntroP2
data.value: SnapZap walks that folder and everything beneath it, recording a checksum, the dimensions, the capture date and camera from EXIF, a sharpness score, a visual fingerprint and a thumbnail for each photo.

data.name: ScanStopNote
data.value: Stop is always available, and it is safe — everything analysed so far is kept.

data.name: ScanUnsupportedNote
data.value: These are counted and reported above the grid, never touched. If your library came off an iPhone it is probably mostly HEIC — which is why SnapZap says so rather than reporting an empty folder.

data.name: ScanFastP1
data.value: A file whose path, size and modification time have not changed is reused from the catalogue rather than read again, so scanning the same library a second time is close to instant.

data.name: ScanFastP2
data.value: Files that have left the folder are dropped from the catalogue, and the status line says how many — along with their scores and keeper decisions, which is why it is said out loud rather than shown as a quietly shorter grid.

data.name: DupeKindsHeading
data.value: Three kinds, and the difference matters

data.name: DupeIdenticalDesc
data.value: Byte-for-byte the same file, in two places. Found by checksum.

data.name: DupeSameShotDesc
data.value: One photograph, resized, re-saved, converted or rotated.

data.name: DupeBurstDesc
data.value: Different photographs of the same scene, seconds apart.

data.name: DupeBurstNoteBody
data.value: A burst of five frames is five different photographs, not five copies of one. SnapZap groups them so you can look at them, and leaves them out of Extras — sweeping them into a delete would throw real photos away. For a burst, you pick the keeper yourself. This is on by default; Setup can switch it off, and switching it off means burst frames are treated as copies.

data.name: DupeBadgesNote
data.value: Cards pick up a badge: ✓ for the copy being kept from its group, ▣ for an extra copy. Hover either for the group number and kind.

data.name: DupeReviewP1
data.value: Press Review N groups (Plan tab, or the banner above the grid) for the good way to work through them — one group at a time, copies side by side. Facts that are identical across the group are greyed out because they cannot help you choose; whatever differs stays bright, and a clear winner on resolution or file size is highlighted.

data.name: DupeReviewP2
data.value: Click a copy to make it the keeper. Compare full size opens them at full resolution with the panes panning together. Nothing is deleted in that dialog — it only decides which copy survives an export or delete you run afterwards.

data.name: DupeTuningIdentical
data.value: Identical files — always on. A duplicate finder that cannot find identical files is not one.

data.name: DupeTuningSameShot
data.value: The same shot at another size — on by default, with a strictness slider (default 20 of 272) and an option to match rotated copies.

data.name: DupeTuningBursts
data.value: Bursts — on by default, with a tunable window (default 3 seconds). Turning it off does not leave bursts alone: the frames are picked up as “same shot” instead, which is bulk-selectable.

data.name: DupeTuningHint
data.value: Changes save immediately. Press Find again under the Duplicates step (Plan tab) to apply them.

data.name: NsfwP1
data.value: Press Run under Content review (Plan tab, or the same facet in the Filters tab). This is the one feature that needs an optional download — see Setup if the button is greyed out. Everything else in SnapZap works without it.

data.name: NsfwP2
data.value: Every photo gets one score from 0.00 to 1.00 and lands in a band:

data.name: NsfwNotSureMeaning
data.value: The pile actually worth looking at

data.name: NsfwGuessTitle
data.value: It is a guess, not a verdict

data.name: NsfwGuessBody
data.value: The model is right often enough to be useful and wrong often enough that you should look before you act. That is exactly what the "Not sure" band is for — it is deliberately small, so it stays a review queue rather than a category.

data.name: NsfwShieldNote
data.value: Flagged photos get a shield badge in the grid; hover it for the score and the threshold it was measured against.

data.name: SelectHeading1
data.value: Nothing happens until you select something

data.name: SelectIntro
data.value: The Export… and Delete… buttons only appear once at least one photo is picked.

data.name: SelectShiftClickDesc
data.value: Select the whole range from the last photo you clicked to this one.

data.name: SelectByCommandP1
data.value: Select all N shown sits at the top of the grid — it picks everything the current filters show ({0}A). Its own chevron opens a menu for a few other scopes; each shows how many photos it would pick.

data.name: SelectScopeFlaggedDesc
data.value: Photos the model called likely explicit

data.name: SelectScopeNotSureDesc
data.value: Photos the model was unsure about

data.name: SelectScopeKeepersDesc
data.value: The one copy being kept from each duplicate group

data.name: SelectExtraCopiesNote
data.value: The Filters tab's Duplicates facet has an Extra copies only row — narrow to it, then Select all N shown picks every extra copy: identical and same-shot only, never burst frames.

data.name: SelectInvertClearNote
data.value: Once something is selected, Invert and Clear appear in the bar at the bottom of the grid, next to the count ({0}D also clears).

data.name: SelectGreyedHint
data.value: A command that cannot do anything stays visible but greyed, and its tooltip says which step is actually missing.

data.name: SelectSharedTitle
data.value: The selection is shared by every SnapZap window

data.name: SelectSharedBody
data.value: Picking a scope replaces the selection rather than adding to it, so a press in one window changes what the other is about to export or delete.

data.name: ExportIntro
data.value: Select the photos you want, then press Export…. Give it a full path starting from the root of the drive — a relative one is rejected, because it would quietly resolve somewhere inside the folder you are cleaning.

data.name: ExportCopyDesc
data.value: The default, and the safest. Originals stay exactly where they are.

data.name: ExportMoveDesc
data.value: The file is written, hash-verified against the original, and only then is the source removed.

data.name: ExportHardlinkDesc
data.value: A second name for the same data — instant and free, but destination and source must be on the same drive.

data.name: ExportByDateDesc
data.value: YYYY/YYYY-MM/ from the capture date. The default.

data.name: ExportMirrorDesc
data.value: Keeps your existing folder layout. Needs a folder scanned this session.

data.name: ExportFlatDesc
data.value: Everything in one folder, with collision-safe renaming.

data.name: ExportCheckP1
data.value: Press it before exporting. You get the count and total size to be written, the free space at the destination and whether that is enough, whether hardlinks are available, and an example of the folders that will be created.

data.name: ExportCheckP2
data.value: Export stays disabled until this check passes, and changing the destination, mode or structure invalidates it — so the button can never be armed for a plan nobody verified.

data.name: ExportRecycleHeading
data.value: Also recycle what you didn't pick

data.name: ExportRecycleP1
data.value: This opt-in box sends every photo you did not select to the Recycle Bin, but only after the export has been written and verified.

data.name: ExportRecycleP2
data.value: Filters do not limit it — it covers the whole catalogue, not just what is on screen. It is reversible from History.

data.name: ExportWhileP1
data.value: Stop is always safe: everything already copied has been verified, and running the export again resumes where it left off rather than starting over.

data.name: ExportWhileP2
data.value: When it finishes you get a summary and the path to a manifest — a CSV recording exactly what went where.

data.name: DeleteIntroP1
data.value: Select photos and press Delete…. A confirmation names the exact count and total size before anything happens.

data.name: DeleteIntroP2
data.value: Confirming moves them to the Recycle Bin — never a hard delete. A message appears with an Undo button that puts them straight back.

data.name: DeleteHistoryP
data.value: If that message has gone, everything is still there. History, in the top bar, lists every batch SnapZap has recycled or moved, newest first, each with a Restore button that puts the files back where they came from.

data.name: DeleteEntryRecycledDesc
data.value: The "also recycle what I didn't pick" option

data.name: DeleteEntryMovedDesc
data.value: An export in Move mode. These were relocated, not binned — so the Recycle Bin is the wrong place to look for them.

data.name: DeleteRestoreHint
data.value: You can also restore from the Recycle Bin's own right-click menu.

data.name: KeysReviewPickLabel
data.value: Pick that copy as the keeper

data.name: KeysEverywhereCloseLabel
data.value: Close the open dialog or menu

data.name: KeysTabHint
data.value: The grid is a single tab stop — <kbd>Tab</kbd> reaches it and moves on, and the arrows move within it.

data.name: KeysIgnoredHint
data.value: <kbd>{0}</kbd><kbd>A</kbd> and <kbd>{0}</kbd><kbd>D</kbd> are ignored while a dialog is open, so a stray keypress cannot re-aim a delete confirmation already on screen.

data.name: FaqQ1
data.value: Is anything uploaded, or does this need an internet connection?

data.name: FaqA1
data.value: No, to both. SnapZap runs entirely on your own machine. It opens in your browser because that is its window, not because anything is going online. Duplicate detection, blur, dates and export are all in-process; the only download is the optional explicit-content model, and that is a one-time install.

data.name: FaqA2
data.value: Not without you asking, and never permanently. Scanning and finding duplicates are read-only. Deleting moves files to the Recycle Bin and every batch is restorable from History. The only ways your source folder is touched are an export in Move mode and the opt-in "also recycle what I didn't pick" box — both clearly labelled, both undoable.

data.name: FaqQ3
data.value: My iPhone photos don't show up.

data.name: FaqA3
data.value: They are almost certainly HEIC, which SnapZap cannot decode yet — nor AVIF, nor camera RAW. They are counted and reported in the note above the grid, and left completely untouched. Converting them to JPEG makes them visible.

data.name: FaqQ4
data.value: "Run" is greyed out under Content review.

data.name: FaqA4
data.value: The optional model is not installed. Open Setup (the gear, top right) — it shows the exact command to install it, and a Check again button that picks it up without a restart. Everything else in SnapZap works without it.

data.name: FaqA5
data.value: There isn't one to press the first time — duplicate detection runs automatically the moment a scan finishes, no download or setup needed. To re-run it later (after changing a setting in Setup → Duplicates, say), use Find again under the Duplicates step in the Plan tab.

data.name: FaqQ6
data.value: Why won't the Export button turn on?

data.name: FaqA6
data.value: Press Check destination first. If you changed the destination, mode or structure after checking, check again — the button deliberately disarms so it can never run a plan that nothing verified. If the check says there is not enough room, the export stays blocked.

data.name: FaqQ7
data.value: It says "Enter a full path, starting from the root of the drive."

data.name: FaqA7
data.value: Relative destination paths are rejected, because one would resolve somewhere unexpected — possibly inside the very folder you are cleaning. Use a full path.

data.name: FaqQ8
data.value: Mirror structure won't let me export.

data.name: FaqA8
data.value: Mirror recreates your existing folder layout, so it needs a source folder scanned in this session to make paths relative to. Scan the source again, or choose By date or Flat.

data.name: FaqQ9
data.value: A burst of shots got grouped as duplicates. Will they be deleted?

data.name: FaqA9
data.value: Not while burst grouping is on, which is the default: bursts are grouped so you can review them and are excluded from Extras, so a bulk selection will not pick them up. Use Review duplicates to choose which frames you want. If one burst is being split across several groups, widen the burst window in Setup. If you switched burst grouping off in Setup, that protection is gone and all but one frame of each burst will be offered to a bulk delete.

data.name: FaqQ10
data.value: Why didn't it find my cropped copies?

data.name: FaqA10
data.value: It can't. A crop changes the image enough that the visual fingerprint no longer matches — that is a known limit of how the matching works, not something a setting will fix.

data.name: FaqA11
data.value: The message in the empty grid names the reason. The usual one: an explicit-content filter over a library that has not been scored matches nothing, because every photo is still "Not checked". Either press Run under Content review or clear the filter.

data.name: FaqQ12
data.value: Scanning was slow. Will it be that slow every time?

data.name: FaqA12
data.value: No. The first scan analyses every photo. After that, any file whose path, size and modification time are unchanged is reused from the catalogue, so re-scanning the same library is close to instant. Stop is safe at any point — the work done so far is kept.

data.name: FaqQ13
data.value: Where does SnapZap keep its own data?

data.name: FaqA13
data.value: In your local app-data folder, deliberately outside the folder you scan, so it never writes into your photo library: the catalogue database, thumbnails, export manifests and preferences. Setup → Forget everything clears all of it — no photo is deleted or moved, and a scan rebuilds it.

data.name: FaqQ14
data.value: Can I run two windows on the same library?

data.name: FaqA14
data.value: Yes, but they share one selection. A command like Extras replaces the selection rather than adding to it, so a press in one window changes what the other is about to act on.
